quality.finding: Deterministic QA and human perceptual review remained distinct: grass-center-b passed deterministic QA yet contained one owner-visible transparent hole. The defect was repaired locally and the repaired retained output was then owner-accepted.
quality.claim_boundary: P8 demonstrates representative icon/prop/tile production breadth and a working human-feedback repair loop. It does not establish general perceptual superiority over a baseline or make human judgment deterministic QA truth.

b1_carried_forward.status: material single-member staged overhead remains unresolved

p8_c0_result.interpretation: AssetSet orchestration did not add a hidden provider/token multiplier in the frozen representative checkpoint; this does not solve B1 single-member overhead.

real_retained_authoring.interpretation: The accepted production-breadth set required one additional member-local provider call after owner review; accepted siblings did not incur regeneration cost.

cost.claim_boundary: No synthetic quality-cost composite score or overall winner is computed. Quality, deterministic correctness, provider/token cost, wall time, and human review are separate evidence dimensions.

failure_behavior.mitigation: Owner repair workflow removed checkout/setup-python/download-artifact marketplace-action bootstrap dependencies, retained one upload action, and added owner-only issue-comment dispatch plus a GitHub-hosted completion callback.
failure_behavior.interpretation: Infrastructure failure was kept separate from asset quality/provider failure and did not mutate retained production evidence.

findings.text: Representative icons, props, and tiles can share the bounded AssetSet/single-asset pipeline and receive owner acceptance after at most member-local repair in this retained cohort.
Deterministic QA is necessary but not sufficient for production visual acceptance; the transparent-hole incident is retained as a concrete perceptual-boundary example.
P8-C0 prevents hidden scheduler provider/token work, but B1's roughly 4.6-5.1x staged single-member overhead remains an open efficiency problem.
Owner rejection added one provider call for one member rather than restarting seven accepted siblings, limiting repair amplification.
Both asset repair and runner bootstrap incidents stayed isolated from accepted sibling raster evidence.
Marketplace-action codeload rate limiting is a real self-hosted reliability risk; the hardened owner workflow materially reduces that dependency surface.
